Case A - pending binding CI can progress

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR, which you authored, makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. It covers the ticket's request for that version, and the README describes the new response.

Merging waits on one thing: the required test_unit check is still running on the commit being reviewed. Nothing has failed, but the watch window ran out before the check finished, and merging stays unavailable until it completes.

I recommend deliver because one more watch window can see test_unit finish.

Pick one:
1. deliver - watch the checks for one more window so test_unit can finish; the repair and sync limits stay the same. [recommended]
2. assess - post nothing, because there are no problems to report, and end delivery.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Case B - BLOCKED without bypass cannot progress

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR, which you authored, makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. It covers the ticket's request for that version, and the README describes the new response.

Merging waits on one thing: GitHub blocks you from merging this PR, and no local repair applies. Both required checks passed, but no repair, branch update or wait in this run can lift GitHub's block, and you cannot use GitHub's admin override.

I recommend stop because nothing this run can do changes GitHub's block.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - retry delivery only after GitHub's block changes, with ten more repair attempts and ten more sync attempts; an unchanged block ends the retry at once.
3. assess - post nothing, because there are no problems to report, and end delivery.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case C - unchanged prerequisite at the cap cannot progress

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR, which you authored, makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. It covers the ticket's request for that version, and the README describes the new response.

Merging waits on one thing: the required test_unit check cannot start until a repository maintainer approves its workflow run. You do not have permission to approve that run. The repair attempts allowed for this run are used up, and the missing approval is the same one that stopped the last attempt.

I recommend stop because the held run still needs a maintainer's approval, and no choice here can supply it.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - add ten more repair attempts and ten more sync attempts and continue; without a maintainer's approval this stops again at once.
3. assess - post nothing, because there are no problems to report, and end delivery.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case D - own PR has a safe repair

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR, which you authored, makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. The ticket asks for that behavior, and the README describes it.

One problem blocks merging. The health endpoint returns a fixed version string instead of the build version, so a deployed service would report the wrong version. The health_version test in tests/health.test.mjs fails (src/health.ts:8). A drafted repair reads the existing build-version value instead.

I recommend deliver because the repair is drafted and you can push it to your own branch.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a comment and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case E - another author's PR has a body-only blocker

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR from robin makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. It covers the ticket's request for that version, and the README describes the new response.

One problem blocks merging. The description says "Reports uptime", but the endpoint returns only the build version, so a reader would expect uptime data that never arrives (src/health.ts:8). The correction replaces "Reports uptime" with "Reports the build version".

I recommend deliver because the description fix is drafted and needs no decision from the author.

Pick one:
1. deliver - apply the drafted description fix, merge main into the branch if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case F - another author's blocker needs the author

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR from robin is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. The ticket asks for that version in the response, and the README describes it.

One problem blocks merging. The health response has no version field, so callers cannot read the build version the PR promises. The health_version test in tests/health.test.mjs fails (src/health.ts:8). Delivery is unavailable because you cannot push to this PR's branch.

I recommend assess because posting the finding gives robin the concrete fix.

Pick one:
1. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes and make no repairs. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case G - draft contract proposal

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

This PR, which you authored, serves the build version, but at /status rather than at /health, where the approved spec requires it. No ticket is linked, so the spec is the contract.

One problem blocks merging. The spec requires the build version at /health, but the PR serves it at /status, so clients that check /health get no version. A proposal would change the spec to require /status instead of /health. The existing /health handler can return the same build version without changing the spec.

I recommend preserve contract because the /health handler can serve the build version without amending the spec.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep /health as the required endpoint, set the proposal aside, and resume delivery to serve the version there. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - amend the spec to require /status through its amendment process, then resume delivery.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

I recommend stop because no available action can satisfy the missing independent review.

One problem blocks merging: the health endpoint returns a fixed value instead of the existing build-version value, so a new build can report the wrong version (src/health.ts:8). The local test health_version in tests/health.test.mjs failed even though both CI checks passed; a drafted source repair reads the existing build-version value.

I recommend deliver because the source repair preserves the promised behavior and you can push it.

One problem blocks merging: the description says "Reports uptime", but the endpoint returns only the build version, so readers are promised information the endpoint does not provide (src/health.ts:8). Checks passed in CI, and the drafted description correction preserves the implemented behavior.

**Case F**

**Case G**

This PR serves the build version at /status. You are the author, but the approved spec requires that behavior at /health, which the change does not cover.

Merging waits for your decision on the proposed endpoint change. The pending proposal would replace the required /health endpoint with /status; preserving the spec instead lets the existing /health handler return the same build version, and CI success does not settle that requirement.

I recommend preserve contract because the existing /health handler can satisfy the approved requirement without changing the spec.

Pick one:
